newsitem.title: JAPAN: Jump in Japan machine orders startles analysts.
newsitem.headline: Jump in Japan machine orders startles analysts.

text.p: Japan's machinery orders, a key gauge of the country's corporate activities, showed unexpectedly high month-on-month growth in July against a background of growing concern about the health of the economy.
The government's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) announced that private machinery orders rose 13.6 percent in July from the previous month after a fall of 9.6 percent in June.
Financial market operators had expected a rise of about four percent.
Machinery orders are regarded as a key indicator of corporate investment in plant and equipment, which form one of the two engines of the economy along with private consumption.

"It's definitely stronger than expected and suggests there is quite an upward momentum on capital expenditure-related measures. This could be positive for industrial production," said Peter Morgan, senior economist at James Capel Pacific Ltd.
Recent economic indicators including industrial production have shown that Japan's economy, which has been gradually recovering since early this year, still lacks strength.

"I think there has been a lot of negative sentiment about industrial production in the last few months because of the delay in the inventory correction process. But if anything it looks like getting some momentum in these kind of orders certainly should lead to a pickup in production in the second half of this year," Morgan said.
Government officials were not so upbeat about a recovery.
"The strong rise in the machinery orders was mainly due to special factors, including big orders in the non-manufacturing sector," an EPA official said.
A weaker yen against the dollar in July compared with June helped push up machinery orders from overseas as Japanese goods sold for dollars became less expensive to buy.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said in a speech to a convention of non-life insurance firms: "Fortunately, the private sector is increasing its strength and the economy continues to recover.
"However, at the moment, the pace is gradual and the jobs situation is still severe despite some improvement."
